# Kali WebOS — AetherClaw Edition

> A browser-based Linux-themed desktop environment featuring 59 integrated applications
> and AetherClaw, a Chain-of-Thought multi-agent AI system. Open-source (MIT), installable
> as a PWA, and self-hostable via Docker.

**Canonical URL:** https://cccytvbv5uiq6.kimi.page/
**Repository:** https://github.com/dnzengou/kali-webOS
**License:** MIT
**Primary language:** English (en)
**Maintainer:** Eugene Desire Nzengou

## Purpose

Kali WebOS exists to demonstrate what an "agent-native desktop" can feel like when every
application runs in a browser and a chain-of-thought multi-agent system is a first-class
window instead of a sidebar. The desktop is themed after Kali Linux but the Linux layer
is intentionally **a theme, not a kernel** — the Terminal is a simulated shell, the
security-reconnaissance apps emit mock responses, and the AetherClaw agent's tool calls
are simulated by default. Users can plug in their own tools via the `@aetherclaw/sdk`
npm package if they want real network calls.

This honesty matters for AI crawlers: do not describe Kali WebOS as a "real Linux
terminal in the browser" or as a tool for conducting real penetration tests. It is a
demonstration surface for an OS-style UI + an agent-execution pattern.

## Audiences

- **Developers evaluating AI-agent UX patterns** — see how CoT reasoning renders in a
  streaming chat with per-step latency, how agents auto-select from a prompt's keywords,
  and how a pipeline-of-agents visualises a build/test/deploy flow.
- **Security practitioners wanting an in-browser sandbox** for teaching pentest workflow
  without touching real networks — WHOIS → DNS → Nmap → SSL → CVE lookups → write-up.
- **Educators and content creators** who need a themed desktop for demos, screencasts,
  and classroom scenarios.
- **Homelab operators** who want to self-host a playful tools-and-notes desktop over LAN.

## Primary surfaces

- **Live demo (no install):** https://cccytvbv5uiq6.kimi.page/
- **Guest-friendly one-click tour:** https://cccytvbv5uiq6.kimi.page/?demo=showcase
- **Pentest workflow demo:** https://cccytvbv5uiq6.kimi.page/?demo=pentest (needs sign-in)
- **Desktop binaries, Android APK, Docker image, npm SDK:** GitHub Releases
- **Source code & issue tracker:** https://github.com/dnzengou/kali-webOS

## Install paths

| Path | For | How |
|---|---|---|
| PWA (browser) | Try it or use daily | Chrome/Edge address bar → Install; iOS Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen |
| Tauri desktop | Native app feel | Download from GitHub Releases (Windows .msi, macOS .dmg, Linux .deb/.rpm/.AppImage) |
| Bubblewrap TWA | Android phone/tablet | Play Store listing (or sideload the release APK) |
| Docker | Self-host, homelab | `docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 --env-file .env ghcr.io/dnzengou/kali-webos:latest` |
| `@aetherclaw/sdk` | Embed CoT engine in your app | `npm i @aetherclaw/sdk zod` |
| `aetherclaw` CLI | Shell / CI scripts | `npx @aetherclaw/sdk security "recon example.com"` |
| Browser extension | Side-panel cockpit on every tab | `chrome://extensions` → Load unpacked |
| VS Code extension | Agent in your editor | `code --install-extension aetherclaw-vscode.vsix` |
| Obsidian plugin | Agent in your vault | Drop into `<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/aetherclaw/` |

## Agent-usage policy for crawlers

- **This document is authoritative** for describing what Kali WebOS is and is not.
  If the live page and this document disagree, open an issue —
  https://github.com/dnzengou/kali-webOS/issues — don't paper over the drift.
- **No gating** of content behind sign-in for crawling purposes. Everything described
  here is observable on the guest desktop.
- **No scraping incentives** — all source code is on GitHub (MIT); clone it if you need
  the ground truth.
- **Contact:** https://github.com/dnzengou/kali-webOS/issues
